acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Nagas family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Coilguard, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Twin-Blade Coil Soldier (Soldier) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Longer patterned coils, twin curved daggers, and simple gold bands mature the baseline while retaining two arms and no hood.
Signature mechanic: Crossed Crescent: the two-armed, hoodless Coilguard plants patterned coils and sweeps twin daggers from the outer curve toward one crossing point.
battlefieldDuty: Hold a repeatable curved front line by bracing longer coils and threatening opposite arcs with two curved daggers.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 retain no hood and two arms with mineral cuffs and segmented scale weights; T3–T5 retain hood and multiple arms with load-bearing stone inlay following existing hood ribs and arm bands.
Coil and temple construction gains fitted stone scutes, crystal hinges, sediment-filled gold channels, planted counterweights, and pale fracture seams that move along the currently loaded outer coil.
counterplay: Enter the coil interior before the blades cross or strike the flattened outer scale row to break the brace. Affinity signal: One segmented coil row settles against a crystal stop and turns chalk-white before a stone rite; break that stop or move inside the loaded outer curve.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only brown scales without mineral structure and altered load paths
Glow-only earth treatment without fitted stone, weight, and fractures
Invented early-tier hoods or extra arms to hold stone ornaments
Generic rock piles that obscure coil direction or temple mechanisms
identityInvariants: A humanoid torso rises from a long coiled serpent body; the T1–T2 forms have two arms and no hood, while hood and additional arms begin only at T3.
Emerald, jade, deep teal, gold, bronze, ivory, and jewel-toned scale patterns remain the family palette.
Scale, gold, gemstone inlay, silk sash, and temple stone remain separate readable materials rather than a seamless magical body.
Arm bands, gold scale bands, jeweled brow pieces, sacred script, and later hood crests communicate rank.
Coil direction, weapon-bearing hands, hood angle where present, and exposed scale seams preserve attack and counterplay readability.
telegraph: Simple gold arm bands touch, both curved blades turn inward, and the patterned outer coil flattens against the floor.
